summary: Francis Vincent Tiso works in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and religious studies. He studied at Cornell, Harvard, Columbia, and Union Theological Seminary. He taught at Columbia, Sapienza University of Rome, the Archdiocese of San Francisco, and the Pontifical Gregorian University.

Francis Wilford worked in Indology and history/archaeology. He was a fellow member of The Asiatic Society (c. 1784–1822) and served as secretary to the committee at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University in 1794.

Francis Woodman Cleaves was a scholar of Sinology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and linguistics. He studied at Dartmouth, Harvard, and under Paul Pelliot, later serving as a professor at Harvard University from 1941 to 1980.

Francis X. Clooney specializes in Indology, religious studies, and philosophy. Educated at Fordham and the University of Chicago, he was a professor at Boston College (1984–2005) and has held professorial and directorship roles at Harvard University since 2005.
Francisco García Ayuso worked in Indology, linguistics, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at the University of Munich under Martin Haug between approximately 1870 and 1872.

Francisco Varela worked in philosophy and cognitive neuroscience. He studied at the Pontifical Catholic University of Chile, University of Chile, and Harvard. His career included posts at the University of Chile, CNRS, École Polytechnique, and Pitié-Salpêtrière Hospital.

Franciscus Verellen specializes in Sinology, religious studies, and history/archaeology. Educated at Hamburg, Oxford, and EPHE under Kristofer Schipper, he taught at EPHE and Columbia before serving as director of the École Française d'Extrême-Orient (1991–2021).

Frank J. Hoffman is a scholar in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and religious studies. He studied at the University of Hawaiʻi and under Stewart Sutherland, Eliot Deutsch, David J. Kalupahana, Prithwish Neogy, Rama Nath Sharma, and Kashi Nath Upadhyaya.

Frank Lee Woodward was a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar. He earned his BA and MA at Sidney Sussex College, Cambridge, and studied under Caroline Rhys Davids. He served as dean at Mahinda College (1903–1919) and translated for the Pali Text Society.

Frank Raymond Allchin was a scholar of Indian archaeology and Indology. He studied at SOAS under Kenneth de Burgh Codrington, subsequently lecturing there (1954–1959) before holding a lectureship and readership in Indian Studies at the University of Cambridge (1959–1989).

Frank-Richard Hamm was an Indologist and Tibetologist. He earned his doctorate at the University of Hamburg under Walther Schubring, later lecturing there (1948–1964) and becoming a professor at the University of Bonn in 1965.

Franklin Edgerton was an Indologist and linguist. Educated at Cornell and Johns Hopkins under Maurice Bloomfield, he was a professor at the University of Pennsylvania (1913–1926) and Salisbury Professor of Sanskrit and Comparative Philology at Yale (1926–1953).

Franz Altheim worked in history, archaeology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and linguistics. He studied at Goethe University Frankfurt (c. 1921–1928) and held posts at Frankfurt, Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg, and the Free University of Berlin.

Franz Aubrey Metcalf is a scholar of religious studies and Buddhist studies. He earned his Ph.D. at the University of Chicago and served as an instructor at California State University, Los Angeles (attested 2002–2006).

Franz Bernhard was a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Göttingen under Ernst Waldschmidt and at Goethe University Frankfurt. From 1966 to 1971, he was a professor and seminar director at the University of Hamburg.

Franz Boas was a linguist and anthropologist. He studied at Heidelberg, Bonn, and Kiel, including under Wilhelm Wundt. He held posts at Clark University, the Smithsonian Institution, the American Museum of Natural History, and Columbia University (c. 1896–1936).

Franz Bopp was a linguist and Indologist. He studied under K. J. H. Windischmann, A.-I. Silvestre de Sacy, and A.-L. de Chézy at Paris and Göttingen. He served as Chair of Sanskrit at Humboldt University of Berlin from 1821 to 1867.

Franz Heinrich Trithen was a linguist and Indologist. He studied under Franz Bopp at Humboldt University of Berlin and Frederick William University Berlin. He held posts at the British Museum (c. 1844–1848) and the University of Oxford (c. 1848–1854).

Franz Kielhorn was an Indologist and linguist. He studied under A. F. Stenzler, Albrecht Weber, and Theodor Benfey at Göttingen, Breslau, and Berlin. He was a professor at Deccan College (1866–1881) before taking the Indology chair at Göttingen in 1881.

Franz Simon Ferdinand Benary was a scholar of religious studies and linguistics. He studied at Bonn, Halle, and Humboldt University of Berlin under Franz Bopp, where he subsequently served as a lecturer of oriental languages and associate professor in theology.
